# Othman Almashaqba (عثمان المشاقبة): full profile

Othman Almashaqba (عثمان المشاقبة) is a technology leader based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Since 2014 he has worked across Jordan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia on technology strategy, ERP modernisation, digital transformation and IT governance. He has led more than ten enterprise ERP transformation programmes, including Odoo from version 8 to 19, and works on ERP strategy at Meela Investment Company in Riyadh.

عثمان المشاقبة قائد تقنية مقيم في الرياض. يعمل منذ 2014 بين الأردن والإمارات والسعودية في استراتيجية التقنية وتحديث أنظمة ERP والتحول الرقمي وحوكمة تقنية المعلومات، وقاد أكثر من عشرة برامج تحول ERP مؤسسية بينها Odoo من الإصدار 8 حتى 19، ويعمل اليوم على استراتيجية ERP في Meela Investment Company بالرياض.

## Facts

- Name: Othman Almashaqba (Arabic: عثمان المشاقبة). Also written Othman Al-Mashaqba, Othman Almashaqbeh.

- 2022 – June 2025: led technology at Alomran Group (Saudi Arabia; on LinkedIn: Information Technology Manager): enterprise technology strategy, ERP transformation on Odoo across several functions, infrastructure performance +20% through cloud migration and automation, IT governance on COBIT and ITIL, technology costs −15%.

- Led more than ten enterprise ERP transformation programmes, including Odoo from version 8 to 19 (Shahwan Group, Romex Dubai, CellBay Jordan, Alomran Group, TOTO Saudi Arabia, Meela Investment), a digital transformation for Mina Hotel in Abha, and an AI-based IT governance and quality platform.

- Certifications (as listed on his own site): PMP (PMI), AWS Solutions Architect – Professional, Microsoft Azure Solutions Architect Expert, CISM (ISACA), TOGAF (The Open Group).
- Research: three manuscripts submitted to journals (not yet published): SSExam, security of the digital exam lifecycle (Information Security Journal: A Global Perspective); digital twins for chronic-disease prevention in Saudi Arabia (International Journal of Healthcare Management); explainable GeoAI for Saudi residential property valuation (Applied Geomatics).
- Languages: Arabic (native), English (fluent).
- Convictions: every technology project starts with the people who will use it; don't put a new system on top of old bureaucracy; change processes to fit best practice before customising the system; the foundation comes before the tool; security is culture and governance; measure what changed after the investment; before scaling AI, define who decides, who reviews and who is accountable.

## Career, as told on the site

- 2010–2014, Jordan: Al al-Bayt University, Bachelor’s degree, Computer Science. It began with computer science, and I still look at organisations as a computer scientist: in systems, performance is not only accuracy, it is response time too.
- 2014–2018, Jordan: UNICEF, Technical support & data analysis. I provided technical support and data analysis for UNICEF projects in Jordan: systems that had to stay reliable, and data collected and turned into reports to evaluate programmes.
- 2018–2020, Jordan: Shahwan, Odoo developer (Python). I built and maintained Odoo modules from version 8 to 13, and integrated the HR, payroll, timesheet and support modules, in Python, XML, JavaScript and SQL.
- 2020–2021, Dubai, UAE: No Errors IT Services, IT Manager, Odoo & technical support. I ran IT systems and data operations, hired, trained and evaluated the IT team, wrote the IT policies, procedures and security controls, and managed the budgets. Enterprise data migrations at 99.9% accuracy come from this period.
- 2020–2022, Jordan: Applied Science University, Master’s degree, Computer Science. Alongside the work, I completed a master’s degree in computer science.
- 2021–2023, Jordan: Marshall School, Smart Rock & CellBay, IT Manager. I ran IT for a school and then for two companies: business continuity, the support team, upgrades, data security and compliance. At CellBay I led an ERP transformation on Odoo 13, from systems to automation.
- 2022–2025, Saudi Arabia: Alomran Group, Leading technology and transformation. I defined and delivered the company’s technology strategy, led an ERP transformation on Odoo across several functions, lifted infrastructure performance by 20% through cloud migration and automation, built IT governance on COBIT and ITIL, and cut technology costs by 15%.
- 2025–today, Riyadh: Meela Investment Company, ERP & technology strategy. At an investment company, I lead ERP strategy for transformation and growth, align the system’s architecture with investment operations and executive decisions, oversee scalability, integrations and data governance, and advise management on technology investment and its risks.

## How he works

1. Understand the context: I start with the business, its systems and its priorities: I sit with the people who will use the solution and hear what slows their day.
2. Set the direction: I turn goals into clear technology priorities, weighing value, risk and cost.
3. Connect the delivery: I connect systems, data and IT operations to the teams and vendors who depend on them.
4. Read the impact: Did we save time? Are there fewer errors? Does the information reach the right person at the right moment?
- People first: Every technology project starts with the people who will use it, not with the system.
- Don’t digitise chaos: Don’t put a new system on top of old bureaucracy; re-engineer the process first.
- Best practice before customisation: Change your processes to fit the best practice in the system before you change the system to fit your processes.
- Foundation before tools: The cloud is a different operating model, not a spare data centre: clean the data, restructure the applications, set the governance, then move.
- Security is culture: Security is not a product you put in the server room and forget; it is governance and awareness from the newest employee to the board.
- IT is a partner: The IT department is not a fire brigade for outages; it is a partner that turns spending into value that enables the business.
- Measure what changed: The number of systems launched is not the measure. The measure is what changed in the business after the investment.
- Accountability before AI: Before scaling: who decides, who reviews, and who is accountable?
